headline: From Eight Years at Home to Guinness Record: One Man's Wheelchair Journey
meta_description: After a spinal injury at 19 left him paralysed from the waist down, Xie Junwu spent years in isolation. Now 55, he holds a Guinness world record.
summary_short: A man who spent eight years confined indoors after becoming paralysed at 19 has now set a Guinness world record for a 25.8km wheelchair wheelie.
body:
A man paralysed from the waist down at age 19 has become a Guinness world record holder—more than three decades after his injury seemed to close off his future.

Xie Junwu spent eight years confined at home following his accident. The isolation was total, a long stretch of stillness and confinement. But something shifted. Today, at 55, he holds the Guinness world record for a 25.8-kilometre wheelchair wheelie, an extraordinary feat of balance, strength, and determination that speaks to a life rebuilt from the ground up.

His achievements extend beyond the record books. He has summited mountains, turning what once felt like an ending into a foundation for a new kind of living. Xie's story reminds us that disability need not define our limits—sometimes it simply redefines our path.
